content:
Investors just watched an AI driven selloff push the S&P 500 into correction territory, as confidence in expensive growth stories took a hit. When sentiment swings this hard, attention often shifts to businesses where the founder still owns the mission and takes the long view. That is the opportunity. This article highlights three founder led stocks from our screener that show how that mindset can matter.

The three stocks highlighted here offer a compelling starting point if you want exposure to founder led businesses where leadership has skin in the game. However, if you want the strongest names, these 29 top founder-led companies are the top of the list.

ServiceTitan is a founder-led software provider for contractors, and according to LunaRodas, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the key question is how that long-term mindset turns a broad product stack and AI push into durable value for shareholders.

"Our goal at ServiceTitan is to build a software factory where AI agents play a central role in all code development, and this quarter management cited features previously estimated to take quarters being delivered in months, with escaped defects down and bugs identified automatically."

What happens to margins and growth if that quiet shift in where the real bottleneck sits stops cooperating with the founders' plan?

If that bottleneck really is moving, read the full narrative for ServiceTitan to see how ServiceTitan's AI push could reshape execution risk and long term shareholder outcomes.

Atlassian fits this founder-led theme because co-founders Scott Farquhar and Mike Cannon-Brookes still steer the product roadmap and acquisitions, and the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that this long-term mindset is increasingly tied to how its AI tools and cloud platform translate into earnings power.

Atlassian develops collaboration software such as Jira, Confluence and Trello, generating about US$6.9b from software and programming, and the business is valued at roughly US$33.5b in the market.

"Accelerating use of Atlassian AI tools, with Rovo now used by over 80% of the Fortune 500 and Rovo assisted actions up 50% quarter over quarter, is tying higher subscription ARR growth and ARPU uplift to deeper AI adoption, which can support future revenue growth and improve earnings power."

What really matters for investors is how a single assumption about the balance between AI investment and future margins ultimately holds up.

That margin question is exactly what sits at the center of the full narrative for Atlassian , which maps how AI adoption, pricing power and reinvestment could decouple Atlassian's earnings from simple headline growth.

Duolingo is a founder-led education platform where co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn still shapes how the app and English test evolve, with all revenue coming from about US$1.2b in educational software and the stock valued at roughly US$6.8b.

For the Founder-Led Companies theme, Duolingo matters because the whole product and brand still reflect Luis von Ahn's personal playbook for turning free learning into a real business, according to WealthAP, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative.

What really shapes how Duolingo plays out from here is whether one quiet shift in how users pay for progress holds together or not.

That quiet shift in how learners pay is exactly what the full narrative for Duolingo unpacks, highlighting where Duolingo's AI tier could accelerate value and where the thesis might stall.
